title: Make-Good Planning Newcastle: Clarify the Scope Before the Cost
metaTitle: Commercial Lease Make-Good Planning Newcastle | YOS
metaDescription: Prepare a make-good brief with lease documents, condition records, scoped contractor estimates and handover responsibilities for your Newcastle commercial premises.
excerpt: A make-good budget needs an understood obligation and a defined work scope. Gather the documents, clarify questions with your solicitor and compare site-specific estimates before relying on a cost allowance.
author: Joe Kelley
body:
## What is a commercial lease make-good obligation?

Make-good provisions address obligations relating to the premises at the end of a lease, where applicable. The actual documents and circumstances need review; a generic description does not establish the work your business must perform or its cost.

For a Newcastle or Hunter business, begin with your solicitor's clarification of the lease position, then organise the site information and project inputs needed to plan any agreed work. This is a practical briefing method, not legal advice or a contractor quote.

## Gather the documents before pricing work

Collect the signed lease, amendments, available condition records, plans, approvals and relevant correspondence. Identify which information is missing and who may hold it. Ask your solicitor to explain the provisions and unresolved questions for the actual premises.

**Helpful tip:** keep a document register with revision dates so the solicitor and project team are considering the same information.

## Turn clarified requirements into a work brief

Once the lease questions have been addressed with your solicitor, record the actual work to be assessed, the premises condition and the assumptions requiring confirmation. Ask the appropriate appointed specialists to assess matters within their expertise.

| Brief item | Information to record | Question to resolve |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Documents | Lease references, amendments and condition records | Which obligation or assumption needs clarification? |
| Existing site | Layout, photos, installed items and retained areas | What needs inspection before estimating? |
| Proposed scope | Removal, repair, reinstatement or other identified work | Which activities are included and excluded? |
| Access and timing | Site access, operating limits and confirmed dates | What dependencies affect the sequence? |
| Completion | Required records, inspections and outstanding actions | Who confirms each item and closes it out? |

Do not assume that labels such as cosmetic make-good or full reinstatement establish the same scope in every building. Use an itemised brief for the actual site.

## Build a site-specific budget

Seek appropriately scoped contractor and specialist inputs. Compare quantities, exclusions, allowances, access assumptions, disposal, services interfaces and the GST basis. Record the validity period and information still needed to replace working allowances with firmer estimates.

A generic rate per square metre is not a verified quote for your premises. This guide does not publish market cost ranges or assume a negotiated cap or settlement will be available.

**Helpful tip:** ask providers to price against the same scope revision and list clarifications beside the comparison, rather than judging only the total.

[Use the FitOut budget planning method](/blog/office-fitout-cost-guide-australia-2026)

## Connect the outgoing and incoming sites

If the business is relocating, include both sites in the plan. Identify who coordinates removal, technology changeovers, furniture, access and any period when the business needs to operate across locations.

Ask your solicitor to confirm lease dates and requirements. The project team should establish a programme for the actual work and supplier inputs rather than relying on a generic notice window or move timetable.

**Helpful tip:** keep commercial obligations and delivery tasks visible as separate workstreams with named owners.

[Use the office relocation checklist](/blog/office-relocation-checklist)

## Track completion and remaining actions

Agree with the appointed advisers and providers what information, inspections and records are needed for the actual scope. Retain the relevant correspondence, photos and completion documentation, and track unresolved items to an owner.

Have your solicitor advise on any proposed settlement, release or dispute. Do not assume that finishing a physical task settles every lease issue.

**Helpful tip:** maintain an open-action register that continues after the move, with a clear owner for documents and follow-up questions.

## Official guidance and applicability

The NSW Small Business Commissioner discusses make-good provisions and condition records in its leasing guidance. Have your solicitor confirm how the actual lease applies.

The linked NSW retail leasing guidance should not be assumed to apply to every office or industrial lease. Ask your solicitor which requirements apply to your premises and transaction.
